title: Personal agent pattern
lede: One person, one agent. The Ping Agentic Control Plane decides at three points: who the user is (Agent IAM Core), which tools the agent may use (Agent Privilege) and what the business rules allow (Agent Authorize). Everything here is simulated.

steps.title: The user asks
steps.what: The user asks their own agent for something. The agent acts for one person.

steps.title: The agent plans
steps.what: The agent uses a language model to choose a tool. The model never holds a credential.

steps.title: The user authenticates
steps.what: Agent IAM Core signs the user in. The token is for the AI gateway: aud https://aigateway.example, sub user.

steps.title: The agent calls the gateway
steps.what: The agent calls the gateway over MCP with that token.

steps.title: Token exchange (optional)
steps.what: Optional, and it depends on MCP support: an on-behalf-of token for the MCP server, aud https://mcpserver.example, same sub.

steps.title: Coarse to medium grained
steps.what: Agent Privilege applies tool-level authorization: may this user, through this agent, call this tool at all?

steps.title: The gateway calls the MCP server
steps.what: The gateway uses the credential that server needs: OIDC, a static token or an API key.

steps.title: The MCP server calls the API
steps.what: The MCP server reaches the backend through the API gateway.

steps.title: Fine grained authorization
steps.what: Agent Authorize applies finer-grained, business-level rules to this request and data.

steps.title: The resource
steps.what: Only a request that passed both layers reaches the resource.
